verdict.rationale: The only security-relevant documentation is in the Agent Skills spec. It says skills can bundle scripts and other resources, and it defines an experimental `allowed-tools` frontmatter field listing pre-approved tools a skill may use. That glancingly addresses what skills can execute. Nothing describes a trust model for third-party skills: installs pull directly from arbitrary git repos and URLs using existing auth, with no documented review, signing or vetting. Nothing discloses telemetry either; the leaderboard is ranked by install counts collected through `npx skills`, and a community member noted the site does not explain this. Missing for 10: a documented trust/vetting model for third-party skills, telemetry and data-collection disclosure, a non-experimental execution-permission model, and a security/sandboxing doc for bundled scripts.
